title: Shooting shocks family; Special Investigations Unit probes police killing of Windsor man
article: Family members of a Windsor man shot dead by a Toronto police officer while allegedly holding a weapon to his wife's throat are at a loss to explain the events.
"I don't know exactly what happened," said Dumitru Coltea, the uncle of the wife of the man, Cristian Iordache, 37, who was shot at his brother-in-law's Toronto apartment Wednesday.
"I talk to her brother and he explain me something."

The province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) are investigating the events that took place in the Keele Street apartment of George Coltea, where his sister Adriana and her husband Iordache had been staying since Tuesday on a week-long visit.
Police were called to the apartment after neighbours in the high rise heard a domestic disturbance.
On arrival police became involved in a confrontation with Iordache that resulted in one shot being fired, striking the man.
Iordache was taken to Sunnybrook Hospital where he was pronounced dead. A post-mortem was conducted Thursday but the results are being withheld by the SIU.
Dumitru Coltea said the couple had recently purchased a home the the Devonshire Heights subdivision not far from where his daughters live.
One of the cousins said the family would be making no further comment to the media at the request of Adriana.
Adriana was taken to Humber River Regional Hospital for her injuries where she was treated and released.
SIU officers remained at the scene of the apartment Thursday to conduct forensic examination.They have designated one subject officer and nine witness officers in the case.
Coltea said his brother, Adriana's father, and her mother live in Romania.
Father George Sandulescu of St. George's Romanian Orthodox Church on Tecumseh Road East said he knew of the couple.
"I haven't seen them lately," said Sandulescu.
"They used to come to church but they haven't been lately."
The SIU is a civilian body that investigates circumstances involving police and civilians that result in serious injury, sexual assault or death.
